steps.say: Scarred liver tissue blocks blood flow and pressure builds upstream. Past a certain gradient the veins of the gullet and stomach bulge and may burst. Measuring that gradient tells who is at risk.
steps.tx: **Hepatic venous pressure gradient** (wedged minus free vein pressure) over **10 mmHg** (ten millimetres mercury) marks significant portal hypertension, and over **12 mmHg** (twelve) predicts **variceal bleeding** (burst gullet veins), measured by transjugular catheterisation of the hepatic vein with wedged and free pressures recorded.

steps.say: Vomiting blood in a cirrhotic patient is treated as a varix until proven otherwise. Drugs squeeze the gut vessels, antibiotics prevent infection, and bands are placed on the bleeding points within hours.
steps.tx: Acute variceal bleed takes vasoactive **octreotide** (gut vessel squeezer) or terlipressin plus antibiotics with **band ligation** (rubber bands on varices) within **12 hours** (twelve hours), using **balloon tamponade** (pressure tube bridge) for refractory bleeding while definitive therapy is arranged urgently.

vis.alt: Anatomy of portal hypertension collaterals with a five-step bleeding management sequence.
vis.caption: Variceal bleeding management: resuscitation, vasoactive drugs, banding within twelve hours, TIPS rescue and secondary prophylaxis. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Waiting for a second bleed kills. In selected sick patients a shunt placed through the neck vein within three days prevents rebleeding and saves lives compared with scoping alone.
steps.tx: Pre-emptive **TIPS** (early neck-vein liver shunt) within **72 hours** (three days) suits Child-Pugh **B** over 7 points (moderate failure) with active bleeding at endoscopy or Child-Pugh **C** (severe failure) at 10 to 13 points, staying under **14 points** (fourteen), cutting rebleeding and mortality against endoscopy alone in randomised trials of high-risk bleeders.

rows: Child B over 7 bleeding, Child C 10 to 13

steps.say: After the first bleed, the goal is never to bleed again. Daily tablets slow the heart and lower portal pressure, while repeated banding sessions wipe out every varix until the walls look clean.
steps.tx: Secondary prevention pairs nonselective **beta-blockers** (heart-slowing pressure drugs) titrated to heart rate **55 to 60** (fifty five to sixty) with repeat banding every **2 to 4 weeks** (two to four weeks) until **variceal eradication** (complete varix clearance) with disappearance of red signs.

points: Heart rate fifty five to sixty
left.title: Drug arm

steps.say: A shunt that drains only the spleen side lowers varix pressure while keeping nourishing blood flowing to the liver. Good-risk patients with repeated bleeds despite drugs and bands are candidates.
steps.tx: Distal splenorenal **Warren shunt** (spleen-vein to kidney-vein join) decompresses varices while preserving portal flow to the liver, suiting Child-Pugh **A** (good reserve) patients with refractory bleeding as a **selective shunt** (selective decompression of the spleen side) that spares liver perfusion and limits encephalopathy risk.

steps.say: Joining the main portal vein straight to the great vein cures bleeding but floods the brain with unfiltered blood. Confusion follows in many, so this shunt is now rarely built.
steps.tx: **Portocaval shunt** (portal vein to vena cava join) fully diverts portal flow with high **encephalopathy** (brain fog from toxins) risk, now reserved for transplant-ineligible Child-Pugh **A** (good reserve) patients with failed TIPS and recurrent bleeding despite all measures and no transplant option.

steps.say: When the block lies outside a healthy liver, disconnecting the varices works better than shunting. The gullet is cut and rejoined, the spleen removed, and the swollen vessels are stripped away.
steps.tx: **Sugiura** (Japanese devascularisation operation) with oesophageal transection and splenectomy suits **noncirrhotic portal fibrosis** (healthy-liver pressure disease) and extrahepatic portal vein blockage through **devascularisation** (stripping variceal blood supply) around the lower gullet and upper stomach completely in one carefully planned operation.

steps.say: Varices in the fundus cannot be banded and need glue injected directly into the bulging vein. When the neck-vein shunt is unsafe, the back-door route through the kidney vein closes the circuit instead.
steps.tx: Gastric fundal varices with red signs take **cyanoacrylate** (medical superglue) injection, and balloon-occluded retrograde transvenous obliteration treats **gastric varices** (stomach wall veins) draining through a gastrorenal shunt, chosen by anatomy and encephalopathy risk alongside TIPS even in very expert hands today.
